question.text: A pivotal battle during the Pacific Theatre was this one, taking place in an atoll at the end of the Hawaiian island chain, in which American forces sank four Japanese carriers. An airport in Chicago is named for it.
question.clue: On the second day of this battle, the carriers Akagi and Hiryu sank, though it resulted in the decommissioning of the USS Yorktown.

swap.text: One of Tasman's many exploits was the discovery of this country, which consists of a North and South Island and whose troops participated in the Gallipoli Campaign alongside Australians.
swap.clue: A rebellion in this country began after a British flag given as a gift to James Busby was cut down by Hone Heke.

question.leadin: This indigenous group massacred the Moriori people on the Chatham Islands. -.
question.text: Name this war-like indigenous group that fought among themselves in the Musket Wars.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: Tourists often laugh when they discover that even Hawaii has "interstate highways," something that manylearn upon landing at Daniel Inouye[ee-noh-ay]InternationalAirport in this city.
swap.clue: This capital city of Hawaii. It is home to the only royal palace in the USA, Iolani Palace, as well as Waikiki Beach.

question.text: Alongside Lorrin Thurston, Dole forced King Kalakaua to sign this document effectively stripping him of power. This document dismissed Hawaiian prime minister Walter Gibson.
question.clue: It was designed to break the power of Premier Walter Gibson and spawned a failed counterrevolution led by Robert Wilcox.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Polynesian kingdoms.
swap.text: This kingdom was founded by Pomare I and controlled much of the Society Islands and surrounding archipelagos. This kingdom was eventually conquered by the French, and is still under French control today.
swap.clue: This Kingdom, which achieved short-lived protectorate status via the 1847 Jarnac Convention. Its final King, Pomare V, was forced to abdicate in 1880.

question.text: The First Fleet of the British Empire arrived at this site of the first penal colony in Australia. It was originally called Stingray Harbour by Cook, but it was changed due to findings by Joseph Banks.
question.clue: Fed by the Georges and Cooks Rivers, its north shore is home to Kingsford Smith airport.

swap.text: Thanks to a quarantine imposed by John Martin Poyer, this Pacific territory of the United States avoided the Spanish flu pandemic. This southernmost territory of the US has its capital at Pago Pago.
swap.answerHtml: American Samoa [or Amerika Samoa; prompt on Samoan Islands but reject “Samoa”]
swap.clue: This territory has the highest rate of military service of any in the United States.

question.leadin: Translation can cause issues with peace treaties.
question.text: The English version of this 1840 treaty asserts that the Maori will give "sovereignty" to the British while still retaining their "property," but those concepts had no direct Maori analogues.
question.clue: The Native Land Act of 1862 struck down the land-selling article, which had been the cause of the Wairau incident led by Te Rauparaha.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about interactions between early European explorers and the Maori: (MAO-ree).
swap.text: This British explorer made contact with the Maori in 1769. This explorer reached locations including Hawai'i and Australia, and lends their name to the strait separating the islands of New Zealand.
swap.clue: This figure, although not trained as a scientist, nevertheless received the Royal Society's Copley Medal for techniques that he developed to prevent his crew from contracting scurvy on lengthy Pacific voyages.

question.text: The Allied capture of Guadalcanal allowed the Allied troops to begin this strategy of capturing less-fortified locations in order to deprive stronger but more distant locations of resources.
question.clue: This strategy eventually adopted by the United States in the Pacific Theater of World War II, which ignored heavily fortified Japanese strongholds and focused on capturing less-defended areas that could be used as bases.

swap.text: Due to a similar story, seven of these figures at Ahu Akivi are thought to depict seven scouts who discovered Rapa Nui. Those examples of these figures are the only ones on Rapa Nui to face the ocean.
swap.answerHtml: moai [prompt on Easter Island heads or Easter Island statues]
swap.clue: A system of ropes likely allowed these objects to "walk" from Rano Raraku to ahu platforms.

question.leadin: This country's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka was nicknamed "Colonel Steve Rambo" after his tendency to quote the Sylvester Stallone movie Rambo to describe a 1987 coup against Timoci Bavadra.
question.text: Name this country whose first indigenous prime minister Kamisese Mara attempted to seize power from Mahendra Chaudhry, who descended from the girmityas, during a coup led by George Speight in 2000.
question.answerHtml: Fiji [or Republic of Fiji; or Matanitu Tugalala o Viti]
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.leadin: Robert Louis Stevenson's book A Footnote to History describes how a diplomatic standoff in this country was averted when a cyclone wrecked all the warships in its harbor.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country whose independence was advocated for by the Mau movement. Germany was granted administration of this island country in 1899, while the US administered a set of islands to the east.
swap.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

question.leadin: Olaf Nelson took over this people's independence movement after its previous leader, Lealofi III of the Tupua Tamasese, was shot and killed by colonial police on Black Saturday, 1929.
question.text: Name this ethnic group whose rival matai chiefs sought backing from the US, UK, and Germany during their 1887 to 1889 "crisis." New Zealand apologized for its role in spreading the 1918 flu pandemic among this people.
question.answerHtml: Sāmoans [or tagata Sāmoa; accept Western Sāmoans; accept American Sāmoans; prompt on Polynesians]
question.clue: That civil war was written about in the book A Footnote to History, by a man who resided at Villa Vailima.

swap.leadin: Lorrin Thurston and John L. Stephens led the overthrow this monarch, establishing a government under Sanford Dole.
swap.text: Name this monarch who resisted the influence of the Missionary Party in the wake of the Bayonet Constitution being forced on her brother David.
swap.clue: A group of revolutionaries known as a "committee of public safety" and led by Lorrin Thurston rebelled against this leader in order to gain rights for citizens born of American parents.

question.leadin: The "entangled bank hypothesis" of this process uses Y-chromosomal DNA to argue against a rapid origin from Asia and suggest that it was driven by millenia of cultural mixing.
question.text: Identify this long-term historical process. Jared Diamond wrote an article likening the Lapita culture to an "express train" that kicked off this process. A description is fine.
question.answerHtml: Polynesian expansion [or Polynesian migration; accept answers indicating the movement of Polynesian peoples or Polynesians or Austronesians across the Pacific/Oceania; prompt on answers referring to settling any of the Pacific, or Oceania, or Polynesia]

swap.text: Bougainville also tried to name parts of this Pacific island nation after himself. The American libertarian Phoenix Foundation funded the Nagriamel Movement's secession attempts after its independence under Walter Lini.
swap.clue: This nation's colonial system was dubbed the Pandemonium, because it was a really wasteful condominium system shared by Britain and France.

question.leadin: According to legend, Halley's Comet was in the sky when this ruler was born, leading to a prophecy that he would be a great killer of chiefs.
question.text: Name this native ruler who unified the Hawaiian Islands.
question.clue: After being attacked by fishermen during a war, this king promoted the safety of civilians in the Law of the Splintered Paddle.

swap.leadin: This man's premiership began after he ousted Laisenia Qarase in a 2006 coup.
swap.text: Identify this naval commodore who served as Prime Minister of Fiji for 18 years. This man forced President Kaimese Mara to resign in 2000 during a so-called "coup within a coup" while Prime Minister Mahendra Chaudry and his cabinet were being held hostage by George Speight.
